surprises.description: Whirlpool reported Q3 net sales of $3.7 billion, below the preview’s $3.91 billion consensus (and the $3.96 billion alternate estimate). That is a material revenue shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 net sales were $3.7 billion” amid “softer North American industry demand.”

surprises.description: Ongoing EPS was a loss of $0.21 rather than the preview’s anchored expectation of $0.78, a sharp miss that also fell below the preview’s older $0.93–$1.01 alternatives.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anchor to ~$0.78–$0.85; treat $1.00 as the stale print.”

surprises.description: The full-year outlook now calls for a 2.0%–2.2% ongoing EBIT margin, far below the roughly 4.0% margin in the prior guidance cited in the preview. Revenue is also now expected to decline about 1.5%, rather than the prior roughly $15.0 billion sales outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year 2026 guidance was cut,” with “revenue decline of approximately 1.5%” and “ongoing EBIT margin of 2% to 2.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists the prior August guidance as “sales ~$15.0B, EBIT margin ~4.0%” and says a guide cut was largely anticipated, with a base-case EPS guide reset to “~$1.75–$2.25.”

surprises.description: Q3 ongoing EBIT margin improved sequentially, but only to 2.6% rather than the roughly 4.1% margin implied by the preview’s consensus EPS and sales. The reported shortfall was attributed to raw-material, fuel, and logistics inflation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ongoing EBIT margin improved sequentially 80 basis points to 2.6%, but fell short of the expected larger step-up due to raw material, fuel, and logistics cost inflation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus EPS of $0.78 on $3.91B back-solves to roughly 4.1% ongoing EBIT margin — a ~230bp sequential jump in one quarter.”

surprises.description: Q3 consumed about $1.1 billion of free cash flow, with no visible quarterly cash progress against the preview’s expectation for Q3 working-capital evidence. Full-year FCF is guided to only approximately $300 million rather than the prior “> $300M” target, and achieving it now requires another $150 million of working capital beyond normalization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 free cash flow was a consumption of approximately $1.1 billion”; “Full year free cash flow is guided to approximately $300 million (~2% of net sales), requiring an additional $150 million of working capital beyond normalization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY guide is >$300M FCF” and “a reiterated net-debt target with visible Q3 working-capital progress is the single most bullish thing in the release.”

surprises.description: The cash shortfall included an unexpected $150 million receivable exposure to bankrupt Brazilian retailer Grupo Casas Bahia. Management expects to collect about $100 million in Q4, leaving collection timing and the remainder unresolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 cash consumption was “hurt by ~$150 million in receivables from bankrupt Brazilian retailer Grupo Casas Bahia, of which ~$100 million is expected to be collected in Q4.”

surprises.description: Despite the cash consumption, Whirlpool lowered its year-end net-debt target to below $4.5 billion from below $5 billion. That is better than the preview’s already closely watched expectation of merely reiterating the under-$5-billion target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management cut year-end net debt guidance to below $4.5 billion from the prior target of less than $5 billion,” with “over $3 billion in available liquidity” and no major maturities until 2028.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identifies a “stated target of <$5.0B by year-end” and says “reiterating net-debt target with visible Q3 cash proof” would be bullish.

surprises.description: Net tariffs were a 225-basis-point headwind, slightly worse than the preview’s reference point of a 200-basis-point Q2 headwind and its expectation of similar Q3 and Q4 levels. This is a modest escalation rather than a major departure from the preview’s tariff outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net tariffs were a 225 basis point headwind in the quarter, driven by incremental Section 232 tariffs in the U.S.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A 200bp headwind in Q2; management guided ‘similar levels in Q3 and Q4, plus/minus.’”

surprises.description: Whirlpool announced additional price increases—7% in North America and up to 10% in Latin America—beyond the increases already discussed in the preview. The benefit is delayed, however: management said Q4 impact would be limited and the increases would fully ramp into 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Additional price increases of 7% in North America (effective November 1 in Canada, December 3 in the U.S.) and up to 10% in Latin America, with limited Q4 impact and full ramp into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described prior increases of “>10%” in April, “4% list increase in July,” and “~5% August price actions” in Latin America, and said Q3 would test price realization.

surprises.description: SDA Global’s 18.6% EBIT margin was well above the 11.9%–12% margin cited in the preview. October U.S. orders were also up about 40%, although management said seasonal demand had shifted from Q3 into Q4 rather than describing the entire increase as incremental demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SDA Global delivered an 18.6% EBIT margin with U.S. October orders up approximately 40% year-over-year as seasonal demand shifted from Q3 into Q4, supporting double-digit full-year growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SDA (KitchenAid) ran 11.9–12% EBIT margin with 16% US sell-through growth,” and the preview expected trade-inventory normalization in Q3.

surprises.description: The footprint program is now quantified at $290 million in structural cost benefits, but most are expected in 2027 rather than landing in Q4. The preview mentioned Q4 realization as a possible bullish signal, so the longer timing tempers the benefit even as the scale and completed distribution-center reduction are concrete positives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Manufacturing and supply chain footprint actions are expected to deliver $290 million in structural cost benefits, largely realized in 2027, with a completed 25% reduction in local distribution center count.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull-case signals included “Amana/Rio Claro/Ramos footprint savings confirmed as landing in Q4.”
